effort.how_hard: How heavy? Each exercise says how many reps to leave in the tank. "Leave 2 in the tank" means you could still do 2 more reps. That is about an 8 out of 10 for effort. Pick a weight you could lift about {rir} more times.

effort.olympic: Olympic lifts are for power. Cleans, snatches and their dumbbell and kettlebell versions train power. Move the weight as fast as you can, with good form. guide.adjust.accessories: Switching off the accessories block takes away every set just for {groups}.
guide.adjust.core_optional: The core block is optional. You may turn it off or change its exercises on any day. You can change anything in this plan.
guide.adjust.easy: Everything feels easy? First add a little weight or a rep. Never skip ahead more than one week.
guide.adjust.edit: You or your coach can turn off a day's jumps, core or joint care. You can add or take out exercises, like more rear shoulder work. You can use the suggested supersets to save time.
guide.adjust.edit_blocks: You or your coach can turn off these blocks on any day: {blocks}. You can also add or take out exercises, like more rear shoulder work.
guide.adjust.edit_none: You or your coach can add or take out exercises, like more rear shoulder work.
guide.adjust.edit_stations: In a circuit you can skip the jump, throw or cardio station. You can also take out a small-muscle station. The rounds stay the same.
guide.adjust.edit_supersets: Use the suggested supersets to save time.
guide.adjust.life: Life got in the way for a few weeks? Maybe you were sick, away or busy. Stop the block. Take the easy week if you want. Then build a new block.
guide.adjust.max: A set felt like your max, with no rep left? Next time, take one set off that exercise, or a little weight.
guide.adjust.missed: Missed most of a week? Do that week again before you move on. Missed one day? Do it on the next free day, or let it go. Never squeeze two days into one.
guide.adjust.pain: Something hurts? First use a listed swap, then cut that exercise's sets by a third to a half, then drop it for the rest of the block. See a professional if it keeps hurting.
guide.adjust.sets: You or your coach can also change the sets of any exercise, on any day or week. The plan is a starting point you can edit.
guide.adjust.swim: Swimmers: when you can, keep the gym at least 4 hours away from a hard swim. After a hard swim week, turn off that day's jumps. Or take out an exercise, or do the week again. Before your main meet, ease off the gym for 2 weeks. Match the time your swim coach eases off. Before smaller meets, ease off 1 week or not at all.
guide.adjust.time: Each day shows an average time. It is an estimate, just so you know. Nothing in this plan is cut or changed because of time. Want a shorter day? Use the suggested supersets. Or take out what the day lists as easiest to take out.
guide.adjust.time_no_list: Each day shows an average time. It is an estimate, just so you know. Nothing in this plan is cut or changed because of time.

instruction.1: *Always leave 1 rep in the tank, never work up to failure but get as close as you can.
instruction.1_bridge: This plan starts with {start} reps in the tank. It ends with {end} in the last week. The coach's "1 in the tank" is where you finish. So follow the number for each week.
instruction.2: **Do steady cardio whenever you want, just don't overdo it... I recommend doing it on your aerobic days, max 40 min of steady.
instruction.2_bridge: In this plan, your cardio falls on lifting days. Do it as its own session that day, or move it to a free day.
instruction.2_bridge_optional: In this plan, your cardio is on your optional day ({days}). Do it there, or on any other free day.
instruction.2_sport_cardio: **Do steady cardio whenever you want, just don't overdo it... Your sport practice already counts as your cardio; max 40 min of steady on top.
instruction.3: ***The lower the reps, the higher the weight... Always go for 1-3 RIR (reps in reserve), aka RPE 7+.
instruction.4: ****When there are joint pains, usually going unilateral and/or getting away from fixed grips (barbells, bars) and going to split grips (dumbbells, kettlebells, individual grips) helps take care of some stuff.
instruction.5: *****If you have any questions just ask me - IG @BLAZECAMP or TWITTER @BLAZECAMP_
instruction.cf.1: *Instead of working to failure, push your limits over the course of time.
instruction.cf.2: **CrossFit has its hybrid style of performance, so to be competitive, you MUST be able to be as good as possible in EACH modality. Train accordingly.
instruction.cf.3: ***WODs will be prescribed by your box or program; yes, they might interfere with recovery / performance, but that's part of CrossFit.
instruction.cf.3_class: ***The WODs (workouts of the day) in this plan are your conditioning on these days. Do them instead of your gym's WOD, not on top of it.

wod.named.isabel.std: Isabel: 30 barbell snatches. Go for time.
wod.named.jackie.std: Jackie: row 1000 m, then 50 thrusters with an empty bar, then 30 pull-ups. Go for time.
wod.named.jt.std: JT: 21-15-9 reps of handstand push-ups, ring dips and push-ups. Go for time.
wod.named.karen.std: Karen: 150 wall-ball shots. Go for time.
wod.named.kelly.std: Kelly: 5 rounds of a 400 m run, 30 box jumps and 30 wall-ball shots. Go for time.
wod.named.michael.std: Michael: 3 rounds of an 800 m run, 50 back extensions and 50 sit-ups. Go for time.
wod.named.murph.std: Murph: run 1 mile. Do 100 pull-ups, 200 push-ups and 300 squats. Run 1 more mile. Go for time. Split the reps as you need.
wod.named.nancy.std: Nancy: 5 rounds of a 400 m run and 15 overhead squats. Go for time.
wod.named.the_chief.std: The Chief: 5 rounds of 3 minutes. In each, do as many rounds as you can of 3 power cleans, 6 push-ups and 9 squats. Rest 1 minute between them.
wod.rotation.amrap: Do as many rounds as you can of the stations, in order.
wod.rotation.emom: One station a minute, in order. Keep going around until time is up.
wod.rotation.for_time: Do the rounds as fast as you can with clean movement.
wod.station.calories: {n} cal on the bike, rower or SkiErg
